title: Product Photography on a Budget: 10 Practical Tools for Sellers
description: Build a useful home product-photo workflow with a phone, simple lighting, free tools, and careful quality checks.

blocks.text: A professional product shoot can be expensive for a new seller. Before investing, test whether a simple home setup can meet the needs of your first listings.
A low-cost setup will not replace every studio job, but it can produce useful catalog images for many simple products. Here is a practical toolkit.
1. Your Smartphone (You Already Own It)
Modern iPhones and flagship Androids shoot in 12+ megapixels with computational photography that rivals dedicated cameras for product work. Stop thinking you need a DSLR.
2. Window Light (Free)
Use a window with soft, indirect light. The ideal direction and time depend on your room, weather, and product, so avoid direct sun and test the shadows.
3. A White Sheet or Foam Board ($5-10)
Your background. Drape a white sheet over a table, prop a foam board against a wall. Done. You just built a "studio."
4. edit-photo.com (Free)
The background remover at edit-photo.com handles the one thing that separates amateur shots from professional ones: clean, consistent backgrounds. Free tier is genuinely usable, not crippled.
5. A Second Sheet as a Reflector ($3)
Bounce light back onto the shadow side of your product. Reduces harsh contrast. Makes cheap phone shots look expensive.
6. A Gray Card or Neutral Reference
A neutral reference helps you compare white balance and product color across a catalog. For supplier assets, request clean licensed originals rather than erasing ownership marks.
7. A Cardboard Box (Free)
Cut out one side and cover with translucent paper (parchment or vellum). Instant lightbox for small products—jewelry, cosmetics, electronics.
8. GIMP (Free) - Only If Needed
For rare occasions when AI can't handle the job, GIMP is a free Photoshop alternative. Steeper learning curve, but no monthly fee. Most sellers won't need it once they use edit-photo.com.
9. Canva Free Tier
Great for adding text overlays, creating social media variations, and building banners. Combine with backgrounds you've cleaned via edit-photo.com.
10. Your Kitchen Table
Yes, really. Push it near a window. Add a white surface. You have a $10 photo studio that produces $500 results.
The Full Workflow
Here's how sellers with zero studio budget actually shoot professional catalog photos:

items.text: Set up: Kitchen table + window + white sheet
Shoot: Phone camera, no flash, natural light, multiple angles
Edit backgrounds: Batch upload to edit-photo.com
Standardize: Apply consistent background color across catalog
Enhance: Small tweaks in Canva if needed

blocks.text: Cost and time depend on the products you already own and the size of the catalog. Start with five representative items before buying more equipment.
What About Product Categories That Are Hard?
Jewelry: Use a lightbox (cardboard method above). The fuzzy edges AI handles beautifully.
Clothing: Flat lay on white sheet. AI removes background clean.
Food: Natural light is especially important. Never use overhead artificial light for food.
Electronics: Watch reflections. Diffuse your light source with a bedsheet if needed.
Cosmetics: Small products = get close, but use portrait mode on phones for depth.
The Real Bottleneck
Most sellers think their bottleneck is equipment. It's not.
The bottleneck is editing efficiency. Even with perfect shots, if it takes you 30 minutes to clean each one, you'll never scale.
That's why free AI tools like edit-photo.com matter more than any camera upgrade for e-commerce sellers.
